correctness.rationale: The defining identity on two radical elements forces the scalar component of P(v) to satisfy ℓ(v)²=0; the identity on (1,1) likewise forces the scalar component of P(1) to vanish. The remaining identities on (1,1) and (1,v) are 2Tu=0 and T²v=0; conversely they kill the entire right side on scalar–radical decompositions, while V² kills the left. Thus P²(1)=Tu and P²(V)=0, giving P³=0 and exactly the stated characteristic-two exception. The rank-r map is specified by im T⊆ker T and an isomorphism V/ker T→im T, giving F_{n,r}(q). A centralizer element maps any Jordan-chain basis to any other with the same ordered chain structure. An admissible nonzero u can be the image vector of a chain, a one-element block vector, or the initial vector of a chain, according to its position; these extensions always exist and the positions are invariant. This proves one orbit per nonempty position, and multiplying its fiber size by F gives the orbit size. Rank 0 contributes two classes and the top rank loses the kernel-minus-image class exactly when n is even; summation gives all four formulas. I inspected the frozen verify.py and VERIFICATION.md without executing them. An independent bounded enumeration of all (n+1)×(n+1) matrices, including arbitrary scalar rows, tested the original identity on unordered basis pairs (sufficient by symmetry and bilinearity). For (n,q)=(2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,2), it tested 512,19683,262144,65536 maps and found 16,33,256,176 operators, with 6,0,180,84 of them having P²≠0. For q=4, arithmetic used the basis 1,t with t²=t+1. This is corroboration, not the general proof.
